close_reason: SWC swap complete. title: Revert vitest.config.ts to Vitest 4 defaults
description: Track C left vitest.config.ts using oxc:false + unplugin-swc to keep the diff focused. Now that decorators are gone, the file can drop oxc:false, the swc plugin, and just keep the test block. Vitest 4's default oxc transformer handles plain TS. Verify tests still pass after the swap.

value: css-url-relative-plugin is load-bearing in this bundler, do NOT remove it. WordPress serves CSS from dynamically-resolved plugin/theme URLs (known only at runtime via plugins_url()/get_stylesheet_directory_uri()), so url() references in emitted CSS must be relative to the final CSS file's location. resolve-url-loader alone resolves paths at build time based on SCSS source location, which is insufficient. The plugin rewrites url() post-extraction to remain correct regardless of where WP serves the CSS from.
Never add 'Co-Authored-By: Claude' (or any Claude attribution) trailer to commit messages in this project. Author/co-author trailers should be human only.

Each lib/services/*.service.ts class memoizes on static fields (SharedConfig.sharedCfg, OptimizeConfig.imageMin/cssMin/jsMin, ManifestConfig.asts/mfs). Those caches survive across buildConfig() calls in the same process. So vitest must run dev and prod test files in separate workers (pool:'forks' default — never collapse to a single test file). Track D (bundler-nes) plans to drop these static caches; once it lands, this isolation requirement goes away.

Decorators were removed in Track C (bundler-tjv, 2026-05-03). vitest.config.ts no longer NEEDS unplugin-swc — class-validator/class-transformer are gone. The file still sets oxc:false + uses unplugin-swc only because Track C kept that scaffolding to keep the diff focused; it can now be reverted to Vitest 4 defaults (just defineConfig with the test block). See follow-up issue for the cleanup.
